title: Public Mermaid Projection Delivery
summary: Turn accessible Mermaid fences in public-scope documents into atomic light and dark SVG projection assets selected by the public Docs Viewer theme.
content_html:
Public Mermaid Projection Delivery

When a public-scope document contains an accessible Mermaid fence, public preparation produces one validated light SVG and one validated dark SVG from that source. The published document shows one image surface matching the active public-site theme, and Open diagram in new tab targets the same variant. Public browsers never receive Mermaid code or the Mermaid runtime.

Current State

  • Markdown rendering retains fenced Mermaid as <pre><code class="language-mermaid">.
  • Managed local readers may replace that fence with an in-memory SVG; public readers leave it as readable source.
  • The pinned Mermaid producer currently transforms canonical .mmd media into one neutral sanitized SVG.
  • Public document publication filters and copies already-prepared working payloads. Status, confirmation, and apply do not render content.
  • Public Docs Viewer can decorate explicitly marked persistent SVG images with Diagram Detail View without loading the manage-owned Mermaid adapter or vendor asset.

Accepted Contract

Source And Projection Identity

  • The fenced Mermaid block remains the sole canonical source. Do not create a .mmd, insert a media token, or rewrite Markdown.
  • Require the same non-empty Mermaid title and description metadata as existing accessible Mermaid rendering.
  • Allocate one deterministic projection identity per document fence and derive exactly two variants from it: light and dark.
  • Record generated identities in a projection-owned manifest so rebuilding can replace changed variants and remove outputs for deleted fences or documents.
  • Treat both variants as one generated diagram family in planning, reporting, cleanup, and verification.
  • Do not infer pairing from filename suffixes in the reader. The public payload carries explicit light and dark variant references.

Public Preparation

  • Apply this transformation only while preparing a configured public projection. Ordinary managed payload builds and source-faithful exports retain the fence.
  • Render both variants from the same source with the repository-pinned Mermaid toolchain, strict security, disabled HTML labels, one font/layout configuration, and the corresponding accepted Docs Viewer theme seed.
  • Require both outputs to preserve accessible title and description metadata, visible content, responsive viewBox, and the same aspect ratio.
  • Sanitize and validate both variants through the existing SVG publication boundary before either becomes publishable.
  • Publish the pair atomically through configured artifact-location ownership. A missing or invalid variant blocks that diagram's public projection rather than publishing partial theme coverage.
  • Complete Mermaid rendering before publish status, confirmation, or apply. The existing publish gate may assemble and compare prepared projection bytes, but it does not invoke Mermaid or create build output.

Public Payload And Runtime

  • Replace the fence only in the public projection payload with one explicitly marked themed persistent-diagram surface.
  • Carry useful image alternative text from the validated Mermaid accessibility metadata.
  • On document mount, select the light or dark URL from the already-applied html[data-theme] value before exposing the image.
  • The public theme owner notifies the public diagram adapter after applying a new theme. The adapter changes only the registered themed image URL and matching detail target.
  • Keep one image, one frame, one viewport, and one detail control in the document. Do not render duplicate light and dark images into the reading order.
  • A theme change performs no Mermaid work and does not fetch source.
  • Ordinary persistent SVGs retain their current fixed URL and presentation.

Delivery Checkpoints

PMP-P0 — Establish The Public Projection Plan

  • [x] Add a pure fence inventory and deterministic identity plan for accessible Mermaid blocks in public-scope documents.
  • [x] Define the explicit light/dark projection record carried from build planning into public payload rendering.
  • [x] Define the projection manifest and stale-output rules without treating generated variants as canonical scope media.
  • [x] Prove dry-run planning reports both variants, failures, and removals without writing.
  • [x] Keep ordinary managed builds, .mmd media production, and source-faithful exports unchanged.
  • [x] Stop for review after the identity, manifest, failure, and ownership contracts are proven.

PMP-P0 uses the document's immutable ID plus its one-based Mermaid-fence ordinal as the stable diagram family identity. Source changes replace the same pair; deleted or newly invalid fences retire both prior variants. The explicit record carries light and dark artifact identities and URLs under projection-assets/mermaid/. Cleanup accepts only exact identities from the projection manifest and cannot claim authored SVG or .mmd-derived media.

The read-only planner is docs-viewer/build/plan_public_mermaid_projection.py. It inventories CommonMark Mermaid fences, applies the shared accessibility metadata parser, reports create/replace/unchanged actions, contained failures, and whole-family removals, and returns the next manifest without writing it. PMP-P0 stopped for review before PMP-P1 began.

Review evidence on 2026-07-25: 20 focused planner, existing producer, managed-build, Markdown-export, and static-HTML-export checks passed; changed-file compilation and repository whitespace checks passed. A real library dry run reported no current fences and performed no writes. Fixture evidence covers explicit pairs, source replacement, invalid and deleted fences, cleanup confinement, and source-free diagnostics.

PMP-P1 — Produce Atomic Theme Variants

  • [x] Reuse the pinned Mermaid executable, shared process boundary, SVG sanitizer, accessibility checks, and configured artifact adapters.
  • [x] Render light and dark variants with one layout configuration and the accepted semantic theme seeds.
  • [x] Validate matching responsive geometry and useful accessibility metadata.
  • [x] Publish no output for a pair unless both variants render, sanitize, validate, and byte-verify successfully.
  • [x] Replace or remove only manifest-owned projection variants; do not touch authored SVG or .mmd-derived persistent media.
  • [x] Keep publish status, confirmation, and apply free of renderer execution and unplanned writes.

PMP-P1 extracts the light and dark semantic seeds from the shared Docs Viewer theme CSS and applies the same mapping used by managed inline Mermaid. Both variants use the pinned CLI, strict security, disabled HTML labels, one font and viewport configuration, the shared sanitizer, exact accessibility metadata checks, and compatible aspect-ratio validation.

docs-viewer/build/build_public_mermaid_projection.py --scope <scope> --write renders complete pairs into the configured working-documents adapter under .publish/public-mermaid-projection/. All affected variants, stale removals, and the manifest are one rollback-capable transaction with byte verification. A failed render or invalid variant publishes neither member of its pair; producer-side ownership validation re-derives every identity and refuses authored or otherwise unowned artifacts. Publish status, confirmation, and apply remain unchanged and do not render or write prepared output.

Review evidence on 2026-07-25: 34 focused planner, producer, existing .mmd producer, publish-gate, public-payload, Markdown-export, and static-HTML-export checks passed; changed-file compilation and repository whitespace checks passed. An isolated real run of the pinned Mermaid CLI rendered, sanitized, geometry-checked, published, and byte-verified one light/dark pair plus its manifest. PMP-P2 remains unstarted pending review.

PMP-P2 — Project And Switch The Public Diagram

  • [ ] Replace successful fences in public projection payloads with the explicit two-variant diagram contract.
  • [ ] Add the smallest public adapter that selects the initial variant from html[data-theme].
  • [ ] Connect the existing public theme owner to registered themed diagrams without loading Mermaid or rescanning document source.
  • [ ] Swap the one image src and Diagram Detail View target when the theme changes.
  • [ ] Preserve frame, viewport, responsive sizing, narrow horizontal scrolling, alternative text, title, description, and keyboard-accessible detail behavior.
  • [ ] Leave ordinary persistent SVGs and non-public compositions unchanged.

PMP-P3 — Verify And Close

  • [ ] Add focused parser/planner evidence for accessible fence discovery, deterministic pair identities, manifest cleanup, and contained failures.
  • [ ] Add producer evidence for dual configuration, atomic publication, sanitizer enforcement, matching geometry, provider-neutral writes, and byte verification.
  • [ ] Add public projection evidence that canonical and managed payloads retain source while public payloads reference the verified pair.
  • [ ] Add public module evidence for initial selection, live theme switching, detail-target agreement, and fixed persistent-SVG behavior.
  • [ ] Verify public routes load neither the Mermaid adapter nor vendor asset.
  • [ ] Review representative flowchart, sequence, and state diagrams in light and dark modes at desktop and narrow widths, including direct detail views.
  • [ ] Run the smallest affected builder, producer, publish-gate, public-module, route, and repository-whitespace checks.
  • [ ] Update the feature parent and durable source/publication guidance with shipped behavior, then close this delivery.

Verification Boundary

Permanent evidence should protect source preservation, projection identities, atomic variant production, manifest cleanup, sanitizer and accessibility requirements, explicit public payload shape, theme selection, and runtime exclusion.

Manual browser review owns palette quality, diagram legibility, theme-transition appearance, narrow overflow, and standalone SVG presentation. Screenshot baselines and complete SVG-markup assertions are unnecessary.

Explicitly Outside This Delivery

  • Migrating existing .mmd diagrams, SVG tokens, or finished SVG media.
  • Theme-sensitive treatment for arbitrary persistent SVG.
  • Public Mermaid source, browser parsing, editing, or runtime delivery.
  • Managed-local inline theme implementation.
  • Reader-oriented export conversion.
  • A general responsive-image, illustration, or asset-variant framework.
  • Changes to public navigation, mobile information architecture, or unrelated theme surfaces.

Completion Gates

  • one accessible Mermaid fence remains canonical while producing one verified light/dark public pair;
  • both variants are deterministic, manifest-owned, sanitized, accessible, and geometry-compatible;
  • partial pairs cannot enter the public projection;
  • public payloads expose explicit variant references without changing canonical Markdown;
  • the public reader shows one image and keeps its src and detail target aligned with the active theme;
  • public routes load no Mermaid runtime or source;
  • ordinary persistent SVG, managed rendering, and source-faithful export behavior remain unchanged;
  • focused automated evidence and manual public light/dark review pass.
